Maximum Likelihood Estimation for the Skellam Distribution

Source: R/skellam.mle.R
skellam.mle.Rd

Estimates the parameters of a Skellam distribution using maximum likelihood.

Usage

skellam.mle(x)

Arguments

x

A vector of integers (positive or negative).

Value

A list with components:

iters

Number of log-likelihood evaluations used by the optimizer.

loglik

Maximized log-likelihood value.

param

Estimated parameters (\(\hat{\lambda}_1\), \(\hat{\lambda}_2\)).

Details

At the maximum likelihood estimate the fitted mean equals the sample mean, \(\hat\lambda_1 - \hat\lambda_2 = \bar{x}\), so the function maximizes the profile log-likelihood over \(\lambda_2\) alone, with \(\lambda_1 = \lambda_2 + \bar{x}\), using optimize on the admissible range \(\lambda_2 \ge \max(0, -\bar{x})\), which keeps both rates non-negative.

The estimate can lie on the boundary, with one rate equal to 0 (the data are then best described by a Poisson or a reflected Poisson). This happens when the sample variance does not exceed the absolute sample mean, which a Skellam with two positive rates cannot produce (its variance is \(\lambda_1 + \lambda_2 \ge |\lambda_1 - \lambda_2|\)); for example, a sample of zeros gives \((0, 0)\) and a constant sample \(c > 0\) gives \((c, 0)\).

References

  • Butler, R. (2007) Saddlepoint Approximations with Applications, Cambridge University Press.

  • Johnson, N. L. (1959) On an extension of the connection between Poisson and \(\chi^2\) distributions. Biometrika 46, 352-362.

  • Johnson, N. L.; Kotz, S.; Kemp, A. W. (1993) Univariate Discrete Distributions, 2nd ed., John Wiley and Sons.

  • Skellam, J. G. (1946) The frequency distribution of the difference between two Poisson variates belonging to different populations. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series A 109(3), 296.

  • Strackee, J.; van der Gon, J. J. D. (1962) The frequency distribution of the difference between two Poisson variates. Statistica Neerlandica 16(1), 17-23.

  • Abdulhamid, A. A.; Maha, A. O. (2010) On The Poisson Difference Distribution Inference and Applications. Bulletin of the Malaysian Mathematical Sciences Society 33(1), 17-45.

  • Wikipedia: Skellam distribution https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skellam_distribution

Author

Michail Tsagris

Examples

# Basic example
set.seed(1)
x1 <- rpois(1000, 10)
x2 <- rpois(1000, 6)
x <- x1 - x2
skellam.mle(x)
#> $iters
#> [1] 25
#> 
#> $loglik
#> [1] -2869.714
#> 
#> $param
#>      mu 1      mu 2 
#> 11.001598  7.217598 
#> 

# Larger sample size
x1 <- rpois(10000, 10)
x2 <- rpois(10000, 6)
x <- x1 - x2
skellam.mle(x)
#> $iters
#> [1] 22
#> 
#> $loglik
#> [1] -28072.52
#> 
#> $param
#>      mu 1      mu 2 
#> 10.042114  6.021814 
#>
